stories.title: NY Developer MAG Partners Expanding to South Florida
stories.excerpt: New York development firm MAG Partners is expanding to South Florida and tapped a former Swire Properties executive to lead the operation, Commercial Observer has learned. Kevin Davenport last month joined MAG Partners as the firm’s senior vice president and head of development based in Miami. MAG is also finalizing an office lease in Downtown Miami, though a company representative declined to disclose the location and footprint. MAG Partners founder MaryAnne Gilmartin made her name working at Forest City Ratner Companies, overseeing high-profile, starchitect-designed projects in New York City, including the Renzo Piano-designed New York Times Building and the Barclays Center. Gilmartin launched MAG Partners in 2020, which has since developed midsize residential buildings in New York and a 235-acre, master-planned development in Baltimore. “The firm has an extensive track record of working on complicated, design-driven, premier urban projects,” Davenport told CO. “We’re seeing a lot of those types of opportunities in Miami.” In South Florida, MAG Partners is targeting office, condominium, hospitality and mixed-use developments, either independently or alongside development partners. Davenport declined to provide further details about the firm’s upcoming projects. Davenport spent four years at Swire Properties, serving as the senior vice president of development, overseeing the Mandarin Oriental luxury condo project on Brickell Key in Miami. The two-tower waterfront development, which remains under construction, has generated $1.7 billion in sales, according to Swire. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: MAG Partners (NYC-based, founded 2020) expands to Miami with senior leadership hire.
Firm targeting office, condo, hospitality, mixed-use in South Florida market.
Track record: Renzo Piano New York Times Building, Barclays Center, 235-acre Baltimore master-plan.
stories.summary: MAG Partners, a New York development firm known for design-driven urban projects, is establishing a Miami presence by hiring Kevin Davenport (ex-Swire Properties) as SVP and head of development. The firm is securing a Downtown Miami office lease and targeting mixed-use, residential, hospitality, and office opportunities. This marks MAG's entry into South Florida after success with high-profile Manhattan developments and a large Baltimore master-planned community.
stories.impact: NYC developer migration to South Florida signals confidence in Miami's luxury and mixed-use development pipeline. MAG's track record in starchitect-designed projects could accelerate institutional capital and higher-density, premium multifamily development in Miami's core submarkets (Wynwood, Brickell, Lenox Hill-style neighborhoods), intensifying land competition and pre-development activity in the next 12–18 months.

stories.title: Northmarq Facilitates $11M Refinance of Park Ridge Multifamily
stories.excerpt: Northmarq’s Chicago Debt + Equity team, led by Kevin McCarthy and Alex Czachor, successfully arranged the $11.26 million refinance of The Parker on behalf of Newcastle Properties LLC, a national real estate investment firm founded in 1989. The asset, acquired by Newcastle in 2019, is a 46-unit garden-style multifamily community located in the North Shore suburb of Park Ridge, Illinois. The transaction was an internal refinance, retiring the property’s existing Fannie Mae loan at maturity. The new loan was executed through Fannie Mae on a long-term, full-term interest-only structure. “Lenders are competing strongly for well-located downtown and suburban Chicago multifamily assets given limited supply and strong occupancy trends,” McCarthy said. Completed in 2016, The Parker is a three-story apartment community offering spacious two-bedroom, two-bathroom residences averaging 1,208 square feet. The property sits steps from a Metra station with direct commuter rail access to downtown Chicago, just minutes from O’Hare International Airport, and close to Park Ridge’s walkable Uptown district. Join us for the Connect Midwest Multifamily conference on the afternoon of Tuesday, June 8, 2027, at Joe’s Live in Rosemont, Illinois. bullets: Northmarq arranged $11.26M Fannie Mae refi for 46-unit Park Ridge garden property.
The Parker (2016-built, 1,208 sq ft avg units) refinanced at maturity on full-term I/O.
Chicago lender competition strong for suburban multifamily; limited supply, strong occupancy cited.
stories.summary: Northmarq's Chicago debt team refinanced The Parker, a 46-unit garden-style community in Park Ridge (North Shore suburb), for $11.26 million through Fannie Mae. The property was acquired by Newcastle Properties in 2019 and benefits from proximity to Metra commuter rail and O'Hare. The transaction was an internal refinance retiring an existing Fannie Mae loan at maturity on a long-term, interest-only structure.
stories.impact: Strong lender competition and full-term I/O terms signal healthy suburban Chicago multifamily fundamentals and capital availability for stabilized assets. Park Ridge's transit access and limited supply make suburban North Shore infill sites attractive for new development; developers should prioritize Metra-adjacent land acquisition before valuations and cap rates move further.

stories.title: The Missner Group Begins Renovation of Northbrook Mercedes-Benz Dealership
stories.excerpt: The Missner Group has started construction on the interior renovation of Autohaus Automotive, Inc., a Mercedes-Benz dealership located in Northbrook, Illinois. The 19,550-square-foot renovation will modernize the dealership’s first-floor customer and employee spaces, including the showroom, customer lounge, vehicle delivery area, sales offices, service offices, and circulation corridors. Additional improvements include upgrades to mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems, as well as the installation of new customer EV charging capabilities. The Missner Group is serving as the general contractor for the project, with Fitzgerald Architecture Planning Design providing architectural services. Located at 1600 Frontage Road in Northbrook, the property has long served the North Shore community as a trusted source for new and certified pre-owned Mercedes-Benz vehicles and service.  “Having built the original building, we’re proud to return and lead these renovations as the market and customer expectations evolve,” said Neely Sadowski, President of Construction at The Missner Group. The project is expected to conclude in May of 2027. Mark Goode to Receive Lifetime Achievement Award at Connect Industrial Midwest on Tuesday, March 2, 2027, at Joe’s Live in Rosemont. Following the presentation, Mark Goode will sit down for a special keynote interview with his son, Matt Goode. The post The Missner Group Begins Renovation of Northbrook Mercedes-Benz Dealership appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Missner Group renovating 19,550 sq ft Mercedes dealership in Northbrook, Illinois.
Project adds EV charging, updates MEP, modernizes showroom and service areas.
Completion expected May 2027; unrelated to multifamily development.
stories.summary: The Missner Group has begun interior renovation of an Autohaus Mercedes-Benz dealership at 1600 Frontage Road in Northbrook, Illinois. The 19,550-square-foot project modernizes customer and employee spaces, adds EV charging infrastructure, and upgrades mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems. Completion is targeted for May 2027.
stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily development. Commercial auto retail renovation; no bearing on apartment demand, supply, capital, or construction cost trends.

Baird & Warner is expanding its Oak Park, Illinois, presence with the addition of Beyond Properties, a boutique brokerage whose dozen agents will join the firm as Beyond Properties Group. Led by owner and designated managing broker Erica Cuneen, the group will join Baird & Warner’s Oak Park office while retaining its existing physical location on Marion Street. Beyond Properties Group represents buyers and sellers in Oak Park, the surrounding suburbs and in the city of Chicago. Broadshore Capital Partners, now the institutional investment and lending arm of Milhaus SRG, announced the closing of a $68.5 million senior bridge loan. The loan is secured by J Optimist Park, a newly delivered 350-unit multifamily community within Charlotte, North Carolina’s rapidly evolving North Davidson Arts District. Emerus operates in TX, NV, OK, PA, WI across hospital and emergency department assets.

stories.title: Houston Apartment Investor Buys 378-Unit Affordable Housing Community
stories.excerpt: Turner Impact Capital acquired a 378-unit multifamily community in Houston and will preserve affordability for low- and moderate-income residents through a tax exemption agreement with the Houston Housing Authority. Under a regulatory agreement with the Houston Housing Authority, the Fund will maintain existing rent restrictions on half of the apartments, reserving at least 152 units for households earning 80% of Area Median Income (AMI) and 37 units for households earning up to 60% of AMI. Built in 2023, Acova Brentwood is a garden-style community consisting of nine three-story residential buildings across 13.5 acres. The one- and two-bedroom apartments feature resident amenities, including a fitness center, pool with a sundeck, clubhouse, lounge, grilling stations, dog park, personal garages and covered parking. TI Communities, Turner Impact’s property management affiliate, will operate Acova Brentwood and offer tailored resident enrichment programs in areas such as youth education, adult financial literacy, healthcare, and wellness to enhance residents’ quality of life, economic opportunity, and tenant satisfaction. The post Houston Apartment Investor Buys 378-Unit Affordable Housing Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Turner Impact Capital acquired 378-unit Acova Brentwood (2023-built) in Houston.

stories.summary: Turner Impact Capital acquired Acova Brentwood, a 378-unit garden-style multifamily community in Houston built in 2023. Under a regulatory agreement with the Houston Housing Authority, the firm will preserve affordability on 189 units (152 at 80% AMI, 37 at 60% AMI). TI Communities will manage the property and offer tailored resident enrichment programs in education, financial literacy, healthcare, and wellness.
stories.impact: Demonstrates strong institutional capital demand for stabilized, mission-driven affordable multifamily in high-growth Texas markets. Tax exemption agreements improve operational economics for preservation deals, expanding investor base. Developers should model affordable preservation deals in Houston with 5–7 year hold windows to compete for similar institutional capital.

stories.title: Metis Equities Buys Luxury Brooklyn Apartment Building for $52M
stories.excerpt: A luxury apartment building in Brooklyn’s Prospect Lefferts Gardens neighborhood has traded for $52 million. Doron Greenberg, a managing partner at real estate investment platform Metis Equities, using the entity ME 100 Lenox Holdings, purchased the eight-story, 95-unit residential building at 100 Lenox Road from Brooklyn-based development firm Pulse Bedford Development, according to city records made public Thursday. Greenberg is also the co-founder of New York-based real estate development and investment firm GO-RE Partners. Metis Equities operates as a joint venture between GO-RE and Vision Real Estate, the latter of which has more than $2.5 billion deployed in U.S. multifamily, according to Metis Equities’ website. Greenberg signed the deal for the buyer, while Ben Beitel, CEO of Pulse Bedford Development, signed for the seller, records show. It’s unclear who brokered the deal. Spokespeople for Metis Equities and EXR, the leasing agent for 100 Lenox, did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Pulse Bedford could not be reached for comment. Built in 1899, the property southeast of Prospect Park was redeveloped by Pulse Bedford in 2020. The building features 95 rental apartments ranging from studios to two-bedrooms and includes amenities such as a fitness center, coworking spaces, bike storage and a parking garage. Greenberg’s plans for 100 Lenox are unclear, but this isn’t his firm’s first Brooklyn acquisition in recent years. In May 2025, GO-RE acquired a seven-story, 66-unit apartment building in Flatbush at 88 Linden Boulevard for $28 million, as Commercial Observer previously reported. Greenberg signed that deal for GO-RE. Over in East Harlem, GO-RE acquired a pair of multifamily buildings at 69 East 125th Street and 58 East 126th Street for $28.2 million in October 2023. Isabelle Durso can be reached at idurso@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Metis Equities (GO-RE Partners + Vision Real Estate JV) bought 95-unit Brooklyn building for $52M.
100 Lenox Road, Prospect Lefferts Gardens, eight-story luxury apartment asset.
Vision Real Estate has deployed $2.5B+ in US multifamily; strategic portfolio addition.
stories.summary: Metis Equities, a joint venture between GO-RE Partners and Vision Real Estate (which has deployed over $2.5 billion in U.S. multifamily), acquired 100 Lenox Road, an eight-story, 95-unit luxury apartment building in Brooklyn's Prospect Lefferts Gardens neighborhood, for $52 million from Pulse Bedford Development. Doron Greenberg, GO-RE co-founder and Metis Equities managing partner, led the acquisition.
stories.impact: Major institutional multifamily investor (Vision Real Estate) doubling down on Brooklyn luxury with $52M acquisition signals strong capital demand and valuation confidence in outer-borough premium rental. Prospect Lefferts Gardens gentrification and transit access attracting institutional capital; competitors should expect cap-rate compression on newer stabilized assets and rising acquisition prices in similar Brooklyn submarkets.

stories.title: Enverra Buys Northern Virginia Office Campus for $42M
stories.excerpt: Enverra Real Estate Partners has acquired a two-building office campus in Northern Virginia in a bet on rising demand from defense and national security tenants. The investment firm purchased Caywood, a 260,000-square-foot Class A office campus at 13221 and 13241 Woodland Park Drive in Herndon, Va. Representatives did not disclose the value of the deal or the name of the seller, but a source familiar with the deal told Commercial Observer that the campus traded for $41.5 million, or $160 per square foot. The campus is 95 percent leased, with a weighted average remaining lease term of 5.6 years. The Small Business Administration anchors the property. “Herndon’s fundamentals are moving in our favor on both sides of the equation,” Tommy Spinosa, managing partner at Enverra, said in a statement. “The defense and national security sector is driving significant demand for office space in the Dulles corridor, while office-to-residential and data center conversions are taking a meaningful share of supply out of the market.” Herndon’s office submarket contains approximately 8.6 million square feet, while roughly 2.8 million square feet of office space within three miles of Caywood is expected to be redeveloped for residential and data center uses, according to Enverra. Caywood is along the Dulles Toll Road, between the Metro’s Innovation Center and Herndon Silver Line stations, approximately six minutes from Dulles International Airport. The development features a 100-person conference center, fitness and wellness facilities, and a tenant lounge with coworking space. Enverra plans additional multimillion-dollar improvements, including replacements of cooling towers, HVAC equipment and building automation systems. The company also intends to introduce a full-service café and an on-site tenant experience program. bullets: Enverra Real Estate Partners acquired 260K sq ft Caywood office campus in Herndon, VA for $41.5M.
95% leased, 5.6-year WAULT; Small Business Administration anchors tenant.
Defense/national security sector driving Dulles corridor office demand; office-to-res conversions removing supply.
stories.summary: Enverra Real Estate Partners purchased Caywood, a two-building, 260,000-square-foot Class A office campus in Herndon, Virginia (Dulles corridor), for $41.5 million ($160/sq ft). The campus is 95 percent leased with a 5.6-year weighted average remaining lease term, anchored by the Small Business Administration. Enverra cited rising demand from defense and national security tenants and supply removal via office-to-residential conversions as key fundamentals.
stories.impact: Defense/national security tenant flight to Dulles corridor and office-to-residential conversion activity signal structural office-to-multifamily conversion opportunity in Northern Virginia. Developers should acquire Class B/C office in Herndon, Reston, Sterling to convert to workforce and luxury multifamily; strong institutional capital chasing defense-tech proximity creates pre-leasing demand for apartments near federal campuses.

stories.title: Extell Acquires Air Rights to Possibly Expand Scope of 655 Madison Avenue
stories.excerpt: Extell Development’s buying spree in Manhattan shows no signs of waning after the Gary Barnett-led firm bought additional air rights in Manhattan’s Lenox Hill neighborhood on the Upper East Side. Extell paid a total of $34.9 million to Hartz Mountain Industries for the air rights attached to 36 East 61st Street and 34 East 61st Street to add some development potential to its supertall project at 655 Madison Avenue, according to Tuesday filings in property records. The 74-story mixed-use tower at the corner of Madison Avenue and East 60th Street is slated to have 154 condominium units and 233,000 square feet of office and retail space on ground floors, with Chanel as a potential tenant. Extell and Hartz Mountain did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Extell purchased the tower site ​​for $160 million from Williams Equities in 2024, and Barnett has been clearing a path through adjacent sites to make way for the Madison Avenue project. He bought 33-39 East 60th Street for $103 million in March 2025, followed by a $39.9 million transaction with private social club Metropolitan Club to transfer 135,146 square feet of air rights from 1 East 60th Street in February of this year. This week alone, three of Barnett’s deals for smaller properties have been made public, showcasing how busy the developer is in his plans for projects across Manhattan. On Monday, a deed filing in property records indicated that Barnett paid Jay and Stuart Podolsky of Amsterdam Hospitality Group $27.9 million to purchase 1645 First Avenue to potentially build a 542-unit housing project on the vacant site that Extell filed plans for in 2021. The same day, Extell filed a deed showing that it spent $18 million on a four-story commercial building at 1190 Avenue of the Americas in Midtown owned by Lighthouse Properties and Solil Management. The building is currently leased to a souvenir shop. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Extell Development paid $34.9M for air rights at 36 & 34 East 61st Street (Lenox Hill).
Acquisition adds density potential to 655 Madison Avenue supertall (154 condos, 233K sq ft office/retail).
Extell assembled $200M+ in NYC land and air rights; consolidating Upper East Side development corridor.
stories.summary: Extell Development purchased $34.9 million in air rights from Hartz Mountain Industries attached to two adjacent Lenox Hill properties (36 and 34 East 61st Street) to expand the development potential of its flagship 655 Madison Avenue mixed-use tower. The 74-story project includes 154 condominium units and 233,000 square feet of office and retail space, with Chanel as a potential ground-floor tenant. Extell has assembled over $200 million in land and air-rights acquisitions across Manhattan's Upper East Side in the past two years.
stories.impact: Extell's aggressive air-rights consolidation signals condo-heavy, ultra-luxury mixed-use development strategy and capital confidence in Manhattan's Upper East Side corridor. Dense, trophy-quality projects compete with rental multifamily for institutional capital and constrain developer land availability; rental developers should focus on alternative submarkets (Queens, Sunset Park, Long Island City) or pursue smaller, high-yield infill projects in secondary Manhattan neighborhoods.

stories.title: Development Site Next to Fatal Flatbush Building Collapse Faced Safety Issues
stories.excerpt: The development site at 2625 Bedford Avenue in Flatbush, Brooklyn, which is next to an apartment building at 1321 Flatbush Avenue that suffered a deadly collapse on Wednesday, had previously been hit with a stop-work order and a $10,000 fine, New York City Department of Building (DOB) records show. The three-story mixed-use building at 1321 Flatbush Avenue collapsed on Wednesday afternoon, leaving at least eight people dead and 17 more injured as of Thursday morning. While the official cause of the collapse has not yet been identified, the building had fallen into a hole left by the construction site next door at 2625 Bedford Avenue, which was acquired in 2024 for $4 million by Judy Swimer and Faigy Fischman through the entity JS1024 LLC and FF1632 LLC, according to property records. Robert Fischman is listed as the owner of the project in the most recent DOB records. Members of the New York City Fire Department and first responders search for victims in the rubble a day after a residential building collapsed in Flatbush, Brooklyn. PHOTO: CHARLY TRIBALLEAU / AFP via Getty Images The developers filed plans in October to build a nine-story mixed-use building with 64 residential units on the Bedford Avenue site, according to the DOB. Swimmer and Fischman could not be reached for comment. Demolition of the Bedford Avenue site began in September of last year, according to news site Clarin, while excavation began in September of this year. Inspectors had issued safety citations at the site in May 2026, one of which was for failing to ensure proper protections for nearby properties. A violation notice from the DOB in April also shows that the developers had proceeded with the demolition while under a stop-work order, as work had resumed after they paid a $10,000 fine. There is currently a new stop-work order from the DOB on the property. bullets: 2625 Bedford Avenue development site (Flatbush, acquired 2024 for $4M) had stop-work order and $10K fine.
Adjacent building (1321 Flatbush Ave) collapsed Wednesday; eight dead, 17+ injured.
Nine-story mixed-use project with 64 units planned; construction sequence and safety compliance under scrutiny.
stories.summary: The development site at 2625 Bedford Avenue in Flatbush, Brooklyn, acquired in 2024 for $4 million by JS1024 LLC and FF1632 LLC, had previously received a stop-work order and $10,000 fine from NYC Department of Buildings. The neighboring apartment building at 1321 Flatbush Avenue collapsed on Wednesday afternoon, killing at least eight people and injuring 17 more. The collapse may have been triggered by excavation at the adjacent development site, which has filed plans for a nine-story mixed-use building with 64 residential units.
stories.impact: Fatal building collapse linked to adjacent construction negligence will trigger increased DOB enforcement, permit delays, and insurance/liability scrutiny across New York multifamily development. Developers should expect tighter construction sequencing reviews, increased site inspection cadence, and higher project contingencies for Brooklyn and outer-borough developments. Insurance premiums and bonding costs will rise; regulatory risk on tightly-spaced infill sites increases significantly.
